title: Blue of You
text:
Thinking of you is blue, like wandering

through a golden forest at noon:

gardens are born in my speech,

and with my clouds I walk through your dreams.


A soft air joins and separates us,

a distance of melancholy;

I lift the arms of my poetry,

blue of you, wounded and waiting.


Thinking of you, of blue temperament,

is like a horizon of violins

or a warm suffering of jasmines.


The world turns crystalline for me,

and I look at you, among lamps of birdsong,

blue Sunday of my thought.
editorial_note: The translation keeps 'blue' as the poem's emotional weather and lets the final Sunday remain dreamlike.

title: The Poet Takes Leave of the Young Women
text:
Young women of most tender waist,

you who walk just like melody

and pass through the greenery

like jasmine burning in the morning.


Girls who lend trembling

architecture to the airs night and day

and with your pure hand sustain

the firmament of poetry.


Adorable ones of fruit and velvet,

where earth begins to become sky,

where sky is still aroma:


Let me, as I leave spring,

look back at you for the last time

and give you this rose of melancholy.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the farewell gesture and the poem's springlike, highly stylized address.

title: The Melancholy Still Lasts in Me...
text:
The melancholy still lasts in me.

Far off in the endlessness a rooster sang,

enlarging the pearl-and-mauve silence

where the blue morning star dissolved.


It smelled of sky, of her, of poetry.

Without turning to look back I rode away.

The fruits were ripening, and her fruits.

It smelled of her and of a secret garden.


I went away, I went away as through a romance

where I was the young knight who never returns...

the house remained with its window,


sunk among absence, at the foot of dawn.

Her hand floated, and I rode away.

The melancholy still lasts in me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the romance-like departure and the repeated persistence of melancholy.

title: The Rose Was Left Written in the Air...
text:
The rose was left written in the air.

Morning wrote it with a delicate pulse.

And, setting its cheek against the window

of light, it keeps its appointment with the blue.


Almost perfect and without reason it meditates,

absorbed in its vain beauty;

forgetting does not touch it, nor does the daisy

trouble it with her sorrow of love.


To the moon alone it stretches arms

of fragrance, and walks with secret steps

of fragrance, nothing more, toward its star.


It exists, inaccessible to the one who sings it,

ignorant of all its thorns,

while the nightingale dies for it.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the rose as written air: unreachable, thornless to itself, fatal to the nightingale.

title: My You. My Thirst. My Eve. My I-Love-You...
text:
My you. My thirst. My eve. My I-love-you.

The dagger and the wound that holds it.

The answer I wait for when I call.

My apple of heaven and of earth.


My forever-and-ever. My thin water,

moaning and blue. My love and sign.

Endless skin. The estranged rose.

The hollow-eyed garden that dreams me.


Stellar insomnia. What remains to me.

The apple again. The thirst. The silk.

My heart without use of reason:


you are missing from me so much in this distance,

in the afternoon, at night, by day,

as my heart itself would be missing from me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the possessive litany and the final comparison between absence and the missing heart.
